subject: math
title: Understanding Ratios
seo_title: Grade 6 Ratio Worksheets: Ratio Language, Part-to-Whole, Equivalent Ratios and Tape Diagrams
standard_text: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities. For example, “The ratio of wings to beaks in the bird house at the zoo was 2:1, because for every 2 wings there was 1 beak.” “For every vote candidate A received, candidate C received nearly three votes.”
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 ratio worksheets: write ratios from pictures, use ratio language (3:5, 3 to 5, for every), tell part-to-part from part-to-whole, find equivalent ratios and simplest form, and solve tape diagram and word problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key and explanations.
key_big: A ratio compares two amounts. Order matters: 3:5 is not 5:3.
key_sub: 3:5, 3 to 5 and “for every 3 … there are 5 …” all mean the same ratio. Multiply or divide both terms by the same number to get an equivalent ratio: 3:5 = 6:10.
body_html:
What is a ratio?

A ratio compares two amounts. You can write it three ways. They all mean the same thing:

Write itSay it
4:6“4 to 6”
4 to 6“4 to 6”
for every 4 circles, there are 6 squaresa “for every” sentence

Order matters. The first number goes with the first thing named. 4:6 and 6:4 are different ratios.

Part-to-part and part-to-whole

A part-to-part ratio compares two parts. A part-to-whole ratio compares one part with the total.

RatioTypeIn the picture
circles to squarespart to part4:6
circles to all shapespart to whole4:10
squares to all shapespart to whole6:10

A part-to-whole ratio is also a fraction: 410 of the shapes are circles.

Equivalent ratios

Multiply or divide both terms by the same number. The ratio stays the same.

Example

Write 4:6 in simplest form.

4 and 6 can both be divided by 2. 4 ÷ 2 = 2 and 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

Answer: 2:3. For every 2 circles, there are 3 squares.

Tape diagrams

Draw one box for each part of the ratio. Every box is the same size.

Example

The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 2:3. There are 40 students. How many are boys and how many are girls?

2 + 3 = 5 equal boxes. 40 ÷ 5 = 8 in each box. Boys: 2 × 8 = 16. Girls: 3 × 8 = 24.

Answer: 16 boys and 24 girls

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing the numbers in the wrong order (6:4 for circles to squares)Write the first thing named first: 4:6
Using the total when the question asks for two parts (4:10)Part to part: 4:6. Use the total only for “to all”
Adding the same number to both terms (2:3 → 4:5)Multiply both terms by the same number: 2:3 = 4:6
Dividing the total by one term (40 ÷ 2 = 20 boys)Divide by the number of parts: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 in each part
Using the difference of the terms (40 ÷ 1)Use the difference only when the problem gives “how many more”

faq.q: What is a ratio in 6th grade math?
faq.a: A ratio compares two amounts, such as 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of milk. It can be written 3:2, 3 to 2, or “for every 3 … there are 2 ….”

faq.q: What is the difference between a part-to-part and a part-to-whole ratio?
faq.a: Part-to-part compares two parts, like 4 boys to 6 girls (4:6). Part-to-whole compares one part with the total, like 4 boys to 10 students (4:10).

faq.q: How do you write a ratio in simplest form?
faq.a: Divide both terms by the greatest number that divides both. For 6:9, divide both by 3 to get 2:3.

faq.q: How do you solve a ratio problem with a tape diagram?
faq.a: Draw one box for each part of the ratio, divide the total by the number of boxes, then multiply. For 2:3 with a total of 40, each of the 5 boxes is 8, so the parts are 16 and 24.

sets.title: Write a ratio from a picture

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to triangles?
items.e: Count only the two kinds named: 5 circles and 4 triangles. Circles come first, so the ratio is 5:4. Leave out the squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to all the shapes?
items.e: There are 8 squares and 2 + 8 = 10 shapes in all. Squares to all shapes is 8:10. 8:2 compares squares to circles, not to all the shapes.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to all the shapes?
items.e: There are 2 squares and 8 + 2 = 10 shapes in all. Squares to all shapes is 2:10. 2:8 compares squares to circles, not to all the shapes.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 5 circles and 8 squares. Circles are named first, so write 5 first: 5:8. 8:5 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 8 circles and 3 squares. Circles are named first, so write 8 first: 8:3. 3:8 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 4 circles and 2 squares. Circles are named first, so write 4 first: 4:2. 2:4 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 2 squares and 6 circles. Squares are named first, so write 2 first: 2:6. 6:2 would compare circles to squares.

items.q: Which sentence describes the picture?
c: For every 3 circles, there are 11 squares.
For every 3 circles, there are 8 squares.
For every 3 shapes, there are 8 squares.
For every 8 circles, there are 3 squares.
items.e: There are 3 circles and 8 squares, so the ratio of circles to squares is 3:8: for every 3 circles, there are 8 squares. There are 11 shapes in all, not 3.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 7 squares and 6 circles. Squares are named first, so write 7 first: 7:6. 6:7 would compare circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 5 squares and 7 circles. Squares are named first, so write 5 first: 5:7. 7:5 would compare circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of triangles to circles?
items.e: Count only the two kinds named: 2 triangles and 3 circles. Triangles come first, so the ratio is 2:3. Leave out the squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 6 circles and 8 squares. Circles are named first, so write 6 first: 6:8. 8:6 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to all the shapes?
items.e: There are 7 circles and 7 + 3 = 10 shapes in all. Circles to all shapes is 7:10. 7:3 compares circles to squares, not to all the shapes.

items.q: Which sentence describes the picture?
c: For every 5 circles, there are 11 squares.
For every 6 circles, there are 5 squares.
For every 5 circles, there are 6 squares.
For every 5 shapes, there are 6 squares.
items.e: There are 5 circles and 6 squares, so the ratio of circles to squares is 5:6: for every 5 circles, there are 6 squares. There are 11 shapes in all, not 5.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to all the shapes?
items.e: There are 8 circles and 8 + 5 = 13 shapes in all. Circles to all shapes is 8:13. 8:5 compares circles to squares, not to all the shapes.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to triangles?
items.e: Count only the two kinds named: 4 squares and 2 triangles. Squares come first, so the ratio is 4:2. Leave out the circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 3 circles and 5 squares. Circles are named first, so write 3 first: 3:5. 5:3 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: Which sentence describes the picture?
c: For every 4 circles, there are 3 squares.
For every 3 circles, there are 4 squares.
For every 4 circles, there are 7 squares.
For every 4 shapes, there are 3 squares.
items.e: There are 4 circles and 3 squares, so the ratio of circles to squares is 4:3: for every 4 circles, there are 3 squares. There are 7 shapes in all, not 4.

items.q: What is the ratio of squares to circles?
items.e: Count: 6 squares and 8 circles. Squares are named first, so write 6 first: 6:8. 8:6 would compare circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of circles to squares?
items.e: Count: 4 circles and 6 squares. Circles are named first, so write 4 first: 4:6. 6:4 would compare squares to circles.

items.q: A running club has only sixth graders and fifth graders. The ratio of sixth graders to fifth graders is 4:5. What is the ratio of fifth graders to all the runners?
items.e: For every 4 sixth graders there are 5 fifth graders, so every group has 4 + 5 = 9 runners. Fifth graders to all is 5:9.

items.q: A garden has 23 flowers. 14 of them are tulips, and the rest are daisies. What is the ratio of daisies to tulips?
items.e: Daisies: 23 − 14 = 9. Daisies to tulips is 9:14. Use the two parts, not the total, 23.

items.q: A farm has only cows and horses. The ratio of cows to horses is 5:2. What fraction of the animals are cows?
items.e: Out of every 5 + 2 = 7 animals, 5 are cows. So 57 of the animals are cows, not 52.

items.q: A class has 11 girls and 4 boys. What is the ratio of boys to all the students?
items.e: All the students: 11 + 4 = 15. Boys to all the students is 4:15. This is a part-to-whole ratio.

items.q: An animal shelter has only cats and dogs. The ratio of cats to dogs is 1:2. Which sentence means the same thing?
c: For every cat, there are 2 dogs.
For every cat, there are 3 dogs.
For every 2 animals, there is 1 cat.
For every dog, there are 2 cats.
items.e: 1:2 means for every cat, there are 2 dogs. The first number goes with cats, the second with dogs.

items.q: A fish tank has only goldfish and guppies. The ratio of goldfish to guppies is 3:5. What fraction of the fish are goldfish?
items.e: Out of every 3 + 5 = 8 fish, 3 are goldfish. So 38 of the fish are goldfish, not 35.

items.q: In a fish tank, for every 2 goldfish, there are 5 guppies. What is the ratio of guppies to goldfish?
items.e: The question asks for guppies first, then goldfish. There are 5 guppies for every 2 goldfish, so the ratio is 5:2.

items.q: A bag has 20 marbles. 5 of them are red marbles, and the rest are blue marbles. What is the ratio of blue marbles to red marbles?
items.e: Blue marbles: 20 − 5 = 15. Blue marbles to red marbles is 15:5. Use the two parts, not the total, 20.

items.q: A fruit bowl has only apples and oranges. The ratio of apples to oranges is 3:2. What is the ratio of oranges to all the pieces of fruit?
items.e: For every 3 apples there are 2 oranges, so every group has 3 + 2 = 5 pieces of fruit. Oranges to all is 2:5.

items.q: A running club has only sixth graders and fifth graders. The ratio of sixth graders to fifth graders is 4:3. Which sentence means the same thing?
c: For every 3 runners, there are 4 sixth graders.
For every 4 sixth graders, there are 3 fifth graders.
For every 4 fifth graders, there are 3 sixth graders.
For every 4 sixth graders, there are 7 fifth graders.
items.e: 4:3 means for every 4 sixth graders, there are 3 fifth graders. The first number goes with sixth graders, the second with fifth graders.

items.q: A bookshelf has 12 novels and 5 comic books. What is the ratio of novels to all the books?
items.e: All the books: 12 + 5 = 17. Novels to all the books is 12:17. This is a part-to-whole ratio.

items.q: A parking lot has 22 vehicles. 5 of them are cars, and the rest are trucks. What is the ratio of trucks to cars?
items.e: Trucks: 22 − 5 = 17. Trucks to cars is 17:5. Use the two parts, not the total, 22.

items.q: On a farm, for every 3 cows, there are 7 horses. What is the ratio of horses to cows?
items.e: The question asks for horses first, then cows. There are 7 horses for every 3 cows, so the ratio is 7:3.

items.q: A fruit bowl has only apples and oranges. The ratio of apples to oranges is 7:3. Which also shows this ratio?
items.e: 7:3 and “7 to 3” mean the same thing. Keep the order: apples first, then oranges.

items.q: An animal shelter has only cats and dogs. The ratio of cats to dogs is 3:4. What is the ratio of dogs to all the animals?
items.e: For every 3 cats there are 4 dogs, so every group has 3 + 4 = 7 animals. Dogs to all is 4:7.

items.q: A bag has only red marbles and blue marbles. The ratio of red marbles to blue marbles is 5:7. Which also shows this ratio?
items.e: 5:7 and “5 to 7” mean the same thing. Keep the order: red marbles first, then blue marbles.

items.q: A garden has only tulips and daisies. The ratio of tulips to daisies is 5:4. Which also shows this ratio?
items.e: 5:4 and “5 to 4” mean the same thing. Keep the order: tulips first, then daisies.

items.q: A bookshelf has only novels and comic books. The ratio of novels to comic books is 7:4. What fraction of the books are novels?
items.e: Out of every 7 + 4 = 11 books, 7 are novels. So 711 of the books are novels, not 74.

items.q: A school band has 5 drummers and 3 trumpet players. What is the ratio of trumpet players to all the band members?
items.e: All the band members: 5 + 3 = 8. Trumpet players to all the band members is 3:8. This is a part-to-whole ratio.

items.q: A basket has 5 red peppers and 13 green peppers. What is the ratio of red peppers to all the peppers?
items.e: All the peppers: 5 + 13 = 18. Red peppers to all the peppers is 5:18. This is a part-to-whole ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is not equivalent to 4:6?
items.e: 4:6 simplifies to 2:3. 16:24 and 20:30 are 4:6 with both terms multiplied by the same number. 7:9 adds 3 to both terms, so it is not equivalent.

items.q: What is 56:35 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 7, the greatest number that divides both: 56 ÷ 7 = 8 and 35 ÷ 7 = 5. So 56:35 = 8:5. Subtracting 7 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Each bird at the zoo has 2 wings and 1 beak. The bird house has 7 birds. What is the ratio of wings to beaks in simplest form?
items.e: 7 birds have 7 × 2 = 14 wings and 7 beaks. 14:7 = 2:1, because for every 2 wings there is 1 beak.

items.q: 2:5 = ☐:20. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 5 × 4 = 20, so multiply the first term by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. Adding 15 to both terms would give 17, which is wrong.

items.q: What is 12:21 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 3, the greatest number that divides both: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 and 21 ÷ 3 = 7. So 12:21 = 4:7. Subtracting 3 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Each tricycle has 3 wheels and 1 seat. A store has 7 tricycles. What is the ratio of seats to wheels in simplest form?
items.e: 7 tricycles have 7 seats and 7 × 3 = 21 wheels. Seats to wheels is 7:21 = 1:3: for every 1 seat, there are 3 wheels.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 7:4?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 3: 7 × 3 = 21 and 4 × 3 = 12. Adding 3 to both terms (10:7) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: 8:3 = 32:☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 8 × 4 = 32, so multiply the second term by 4 too: 3 × 4 = 12. Adding 24 to both terms would give 27, which is wrong.

items.q: Which ratio is not equivalent to 3:6?
items.e: 3:6 simplifies to 1:2. 6:12 and 15:30 are 3:6 with both terms multiplied by the same number. 6:9 adds 3 to both terms, so it is not equivalent.

items.q: What is 12:10 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 2, the greatest number that divides both: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 and 10 ÷ 2 = 5. So 12:10 = 6:5. Subtracting 2 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: What is 35:49 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 7, the greatest number that divides both: 35 ÷ 7 = 5 and 49 ÷ 7 = 7. So 35:49 = 5:7. Subtracting 7 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: 5:9 = 40:☐. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 5 × 8 = 40, so multiply the second term by 8 too: 9 × 8 = 72. Adding 35 to both terms would give 44, which is wrong.

items.q: 3:2 = ☐:16. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 2 × 8 = 16, so multiply the first term by 8 too: 3 × 8 = 24. Adding 14 to both terms would give 17, which is wrong.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 1:8?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 6: 1 × 6 = 6 and 8 × 6 = 48. Adding 6 to both terms (7:14) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 8:1?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 2: 8 × 2 = 16 and 1 × 2 = 2. Adding 2 to both terms (10:3) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is not equivalent to 15:18?
items.e: 15:18 simplifies to 5:6. 60:72 and 75:90 are 15:18 with both terms multiplied by the same number. 17:20 adds 2 to both terms, so it is not equivalent.

items.q: Which pair of ratios is equivalent?
items.e: 20:25 and 8:10 both simplify to 4:5. Adding the same number to both terms, or switching the order, makes a different ratio.

items.q: What is 15:9 in simplest form?
items.e: Divide both terms by 3, the greatest number that divides both: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. So 15:9 = 5:3. Subtracting 3 from each term does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 1:3?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number, 5: 1 × 5 = 5 and 3 × 5 = 15. Adding 5 to both terms (6:8) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: Which two ratios are equivalent to each other?
items.e: 10:8 and 15:12 both simplify to 5:4. Adding the same number to both terms, or switching the order, makes a different ratio.

sets.title: Tape diagrams: find the parts and the total

items.q: The ratio of drummers to trumpet players in a school band is 3:2. There are 30 drummers. How many band members are there in all?
items.e: Each part is 30 ÷ 3 = 10. There are 3 + 2 = 5 parts in all: 5 × 10 = 50.

items.q: The tape diagram shows the ratio of cats to dogs in an animal shelter. Every box stands for the same number. How many animals are there in all?
items.e: Every box is 9. There are 6 + 1 = 7 boxes: 7 × 9 = 63. Count the boxes in both rows, not only the top row.

items.q: The ratio of tulips to daisies in a garden is 5:2. There are 50 tulips. How many daisies are there?
items.e: Tulips fill 5 equal parts, so each part is 50 ÷ 5 = 10. Daisies are 2 parts: 2 × 10 = 20. Adding the same number to both terms does not work.

items.q: Omar and Mia share $96 in the ratio 5:3. How much money does Mia get?
items.e: There are 5 + 3 = 8 equal parts. Each part is $96 ÷ 8 = $12. Mia: 3 × $12 = $36.

items.q: The ratio of girls to boys in a class is 2:3. There are 10 students in all. How many boys are there?
items.e: There are 2 + 3 = 5 equal parts. Each part is 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Boys: 3 × 2 = 6 boys.

items.q: The ratio of apples to oranges in a fruit bowl is 2:1. There are 24 apples. How many pieces of fruit are there in all?
items.e: Each part is 24 ÷ 2 = 12. There are 2 + 1 = 3 parts in all: 3 × 12 = 36.

items.q: Kai and Grace share $48 in the ratio 5:1. How much money does Kai get?
items.e: There are 5 + 1 = 6 equal parts. Each part is $48 ÷ 6 = $8. Kai: 5 × $8 = $40.

items.q: The ratio of goldfish to guppies in a fish tank is 2:5. There are 8 goldfish. How many guppies are there?
items.e: Goldfish fill 2 equal parts, so each part is 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Guppies are 5 parts: 5 × 4 = 20. Adding the same number to both terms does not work.

items.q: The tape diagram shows the ratio of cows to horses in a farm. Every box stands for the same number. How many animals are there in all?
items.e: Every box is 5. There are 4 + 5 = 9 boxes: 9 × 5 = 45. Count the boxes in both rows, not only the top row.

items.q: The tape diagram shows the ratio of goldfish to guppies in a fish tank. Every box stands for the same number. How many fish are there in all?
items.e: Every box is 9. There are 3 + 4 = 7 boxes: 7 × 9 = 63. Count the boxes in both rows, not only the top row.

items.q: The ratio of cows to horses on a farm is 1:7. There are 32 animals in all. How many horses are there?
items.e: There are 1 + 7 = 8 equal parts. Each part is 32 ÷ 8 = 4. Horses: 7 × 4 = 28 horses.

items.q: The ratio of red peppers to green peppers in a basket is 2:7. There are 45 peppers in all. How many red peppers are there?
items.e: There are 2 + 7 = 9 equal parts. Each part is 45 ÷ 9 = 5. Red peppers: 2 × 5 = 10 red peppers.

items.q: The ratio of cats to dogs in an animal shelter is 3:1. There are 12 cats. How many dogs are there?
items.e: Cats fill 3 equal parts, so each part is 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Dogs are 1 part: 1 × 4 = 4. Adding the same number to both terms does not work.

items.q: The ratio of red marbles to blue marbles in a bag is 2:3. There are 20 red marbles. How many marbles are there in all?
items.e: Each part is 20 ÷ 2 = 10. There are 2 + 3 = 5 parts in all: 5 × 10 = 50.

items.q: The ratio of cars to trucks in a parking lot is 6:1. There are 70 vehicles in all. How many cars are there?
items.e: There are 6 + 1 = 7 equal parts. Each part is 70 ÷ 7 = 10. Cars: 6 × 10 = 60 cars.

items.q: The ratio of novels to comic books on a bookshelf is 3:2. There are 6 novels. How many comic books are there?
items.e: Novels fill 3 equal parts, so each part is 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Comic books are 2 parts: 2 × 2 = 4. Adding the same number to both terms does not work.

items.q: The ratio of red peppers to green peppers in a basket is 2:7. There are 15 more green peppers than red peppers. How many red peppers are there?
items.e: Green peppers have 7 − 2 = 5 more parts than red peppers. Those 5 parts are 15, so each part is 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Red peppers: 6, green peppers: 21. So the answer is 6 red peppers.

items.q: The ratio of girls to boys in a class is 2:5. There are 6 more boys than girls. How many boys are there?
items.e: Boys have 5 − 2 = 3 more parts than girls. Those 3 parts are 6, so each part is 6 ÷ 3 = 2. Girls: 4, boys: 10. So the answer is 10 boys.

items.q: The ratio of sixth graders to fifth graders in a running club is 3:1. There are 27 sixth graders. How many fifth graders are there?
items.e: Sixth graders fill 3 equal parts, so each part is 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Fifth graders are 1 part: 1 × 9 = 9. Adding the same number to both terms does not work.

items.q: The ratio of cars to trucks in a parking lot is 3:5. There are 16 more trucks than cars. How many vehicles are there in all?
items.e: Trucks have 5 − 3 = 2 more parts than cars. Those 2 parts are 16, so each part is 16 ÷ 2 = 8. Cars: 24, trucks: 40. So the answer is 64 vehicles.

items.q: A banana bread recipe uses 3 bananas for every 2 cups of oats. Eli has 12 bananas and uses all of them. How many cups of oats does he need?
items.e: 12 bananas is 4 groups of 3. Oats: 4 × 2 = 8 cups. The ratio stays 3:2 because both terms are multiplied by 4.

items.q: A lemonade recipe uses 1 cup of lemon juice for every 4 cups of water. A big jug holds 30 cups of lemonade. How many cups of lemon juice are in the jug?
items.e: Each batch has 1 + 4 = 5 cups. 30 ÷ 5 = 6 batches, so there are 6 × 1 = 6 cups of lemon juice.

items.q: A parking lot has 18 cars and 30 trucks. What is the ratio of trucks to cars in simplest form?
items.e: Trucks to cars is 30:18. Divide both terms by 6: 5:3.

items.q: For every 2 shots Emma makes in basketball practice, she misses 3. She made 10 shots. How many shots did she miss?
items.e: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 groups. Each group has 3 misses: 5 × 3 = 15 shots.

items.q: A trail mix has 2 cups of raisins for every 5 cups of peanuts. How many cups of raisins go with 20 cups of peanuts?
items.e: 20 ÷ 5 = 4, so there are 4 groups. Raisins: 4 × 2 = 8 cups. Subtracting 3 from both terms does not keep the ratio.

items.q: To make green paint, Sofia mixes 2 cups of blue paint for every 3 cups of yellow paint. She uses 12 cups of blue. How much yellow paint does she need?
items.e: 12 ÷ 2 = 6, so she has 6 groups. Yellow: 6 × 3 = 18 cups. 12 + 1 = 13 keeps the same difference, not the same ratio.

items.q: A soccer team has a ratio of wins to losses of 7:3. It played 30 games with no ties. How many games did it win?
items.e: 7 + 3 = 10 parts. Each part is 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Wins: 7 × 3 = 21.

items.q: The ratio of wings to beaks in the bird house at the zoo is 2:1. There are 42 wings. How many beaks are there?
items.e: For every 2 wings, there is 1 beak. 42 ÷ 2 = 21 beaks.

items.q: For a party, the ratio of juice boxes to water bottles is 3:1. There are 24 drinks in all. How many are juice boxes?
items.e: 3 + 1 = 4 parts. Each part is 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Juice boxes: 3 × 6 = 18.

items.q: At a school, the ratio of students who walk to students who ride the bus is 2:5. 25 students ride the bus. How many students walk?
items.e: 25 ÷ 5 = 5, so each part is 5. Walkers: 2 × 5 = 10. Taking 3 away from 25 does not keep the ratio.

items.q: A class has 35 students. The ratio of boys to girls is 3:4. How many more girls than boys are in the class?
items.e: There are 3 + 4 = 7 parts, so each part is 35 ÷ 7 = 5. Boys: 3 × 5 = 15. Girls: 4 × 5 = 20. 20 − 15 = 5 more girls.

items.q: A swim team has 18 players. The ratio of girls to boys is 4:5. How many girls are on the team?
items.e: 4 + 5 = 9 parts. Each part is 18 ÷ 9 = 2. Girls: 4 × 2 = 8. The team is not split in half, because the ratio is not 1:1.

items.q: A pancake recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of milk. Lily uses 15 cups of flour. How much milk does she need?
items.e: 15 cups of flour is 5 groups of 3 cups (15 ÷ 3 = 5). Milk: 5 × 2 = 10 cups. Adding the same amount to both (15 − 3 + 2 = 14) does not keep the ratio.

items.q: In a class of 28 students, 12 wear glasses and the rest do not. What is the ratio of students with glasses to students without glasses, in simplest form?
items.e: Without glasses: 28 − 12 = 16. With to without is 12:16. Divide both by 4: 3:4.

items.q: Light blue paint is 1 part blue to 4 parts white. Sam has 3 cups of blue paint and uses all of it. How many cups of light blue paint can he make?
items.e: White: 4 × 3 = 12 cups. Light blue paint is blue and white together: 3 + 12 = 15 cups.

items.q: Orange paint is 1 part red to 3 parts yellow. A painter needs 16 cups of orange paint. How many cups of yellow paint does the painter use?
items.e: 1 + 3 = 4 parts. Each part is 16 ÷ 4 = 4 cups. Yellow is 3 parts: 3 × 4 = 12 cups.

items.q: Pink paint is made with 1 cup of red paint for every 3 cups of white paint. Which mix makes the same shade of pink?
items.e: The same shade needs an equivalent ratio. Multiply both amounts by 2: 1 × 2 = 2 and 3 × 2 = 6. Adding 2 cups to each changes the shade.

items.q: In a school election, for every vote Candidate A got, Candidate C got 3 votes. Candidate C got 63 votes. How many votes did Candidate A get?
items.e: The ratio of A’s votes to C’s votes is 1:3. 63 ÷ 3 = 21, so Candidate A got 21 votes.

items.q: The ratio of points Leo scored to points Maya scored this season is 3:2. Leo scored 4 more points than Maya. How many points did Leo score?
items.e: 3 − 2 = 1 part is the difference, so each part is 4. Leo: 3 × 4 = 12 points.

items.q: On a field trip, the ratio of students to teachers is 8:1. There are 72 students. How many teachers are there?
items.e: For every 8 students, there is 1 teacher. 72 ÷ 8 = 9 groups, so there are 9 teachers. Do not multiply (72 × 8), and do not divide by 9: the 72 are only the students.
